categories.name: Amazon's AWS Certified Developer - Associate DVA-C02

questions.content:
A developer is building a serverless application that is based on AWS Lambda.
The developer initializes the AWS software development kit (SDK) outside of the
Lambda handler function.

What is the PRIMARY benefit of this action?

answers.content: Improves legibility and stylistic convention
answers.explanation: Improving legibility and stylistic convention is not the primary benefit of initializing SDK outside the handler.

answers.content: Takes advantage of runtime environment reuse
answers.explanation: Initializing the AWS SDK outside the Lambda handler function takes advantage of the Lambda runtime environment reuse, which can improve performance by avoiding repeated initialization on every invocation.

answers.content: Provides better error handling
answers.explanation: Providing better error handling is unrelated to the placement of SDK initialization.

answers.content: Creates a new SDK instance for each invocation
answers.explanation: Creating a new SDK instance for each invocation is what happens if initialized inside the handler, not outside.

questions.content:
A company is using Amazon RDS as the backend database for its application. After
a recent marketing campaign, a surge of read requests to the database increased
the latency of data retrieval from the database. The company has decided to
implement a caching layer in front of the database. The cached content must be
encrypted and must be highly available.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Amazon CloudFront
answers.explanation: CloudFront is a CDN, not a caching layer for RDS and does not guarantee encrypted cache or high availability in this context.

answers.content: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
answers.explanation: Memcached does not support encryption, failing the encryption requirement.

answers.content: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in cluster mode
answers.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis supports encryption of data in transit and at rest, meeting the requirement for encrypted caching. ElastiCache for Redis supports cluster mode, which provides high availability and scalability. Memcached does not support encryption, so it does not meet the encryption requirement. CloudFront is a CDN, not designed for caching database queries directly and does not provide the required encryption or database caching features. DAX is specific to DynamoDB and cannot be used as a caching layer for Amazon RDS.

answers.content: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
answers.explanation: DAX is specific for DynamoDB and cannot be used with RDS databases.

questions.content:
A developer at a company recently created a serverless application to process
and show data from business reports. The application's user interface (UI)
allows users to select and start processing the files. The UI displays a message
when the result is available to view. The application uses AWS Step Functions
with AWS Lambda functions to process the files. The developer used Amazon API
Gateway and Lambda functions to create an API to support the UI.

The company's UI team reports that the request to process a file is often
returning timeout errors because of the size or complexity of the files. The UI
team wants the API to provide an immediate response so that the UI can display a
message while the files are being processed. The backend process that is invoked
by the API needs to send an email message when the report processing is
complete.

What should the developer do to configure the API to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Change the API Gateway route to add an X-Amz-Invocation-Type header with a static value of 'Event' in the integration request. Deploy the API Gateway stage to apply the changes.
answers.explanation: API Gateway supports asynchronous invocation of Lambda functions by adding the X-Amz-Invocation-Type header with the value 'Event', which allows API Gateway to return an immediate response while the Lambda processes the request in the background. This approach meets the requirement of providing an immediate response to the UI and enables the backend process to continue processing files asynchronously and send an email upon completion, following AWS best practices for asynchronous Lambda invocation. Changing the API Gateway timeout or Lambda function timeout does not solve the issue of immediate response for long-running processes. Headers like X-Amz-Target with 'Async' are not valid in this context for asynchronous invocation.

answers.content: Change the configuration of the Lambda function that implements the request to process a file. Configure the maximum age of the event so that the Lambda function will run asynchronously.
answers.explanation: No Lambda configuration exists for 'maximum age of the event' to enable asynchronous execution; this is not a valid method.

answers.content: Change the API Gateway timeout value to match the Lambda function timeout value. Deploy the API Gateway stage to apply the changes.
answers.explanation: Increasing timeout values only delays the timeout but does not provide an immediate response, failing to meet UI requirements.

answers.content: Change the API Gateway route to add an X-Amz-Target header with a static value of 'Async' in the integration request. Deploy the API Gateway stage to apply the changes.
answers.explanation: X-Amz-Target with 'Async' is not a valid header to trigger asynchronous Lambda invocation via API Gateway.

questions.content:
A developer has an application that is composed of many different AWS Lambda
functions. The Lambda functions all use some of the same dependencies. To avoid
security issues, the developer is constantly updating the dependencies of all of
the Lambda functions. The result is duplicated effort for each function.

How can the developer keep the dependencies of the Lambda functions up to date
with the LEAST additional complexity?

answers.content: Define a maintenance window for the Lambda functions to ensure that the functions get updated copies of the dependencies.
answers.explanation: A maintenance window does not address the root cause of duplicated dependencies and increases complexity without leveraging managed features.

answers.content: Upgrade the Lambda functions to the most recent runtime version.
answers.explanation: Upgrading the runtime does not directly solve the problem of managing shared dependencies across multiple functions.

answers.content: Define a Lambda layer that contains all of the shared dependencies.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda layer allows the developer to package all shared dependencies into a single archive that can be referenced by multiple Lambda functions. This approach reduces duplication, keeps deployment packages smaller and more organized, and simplifies updates to dependencies across all functions. AWS best practices recommend using managed features like Lambda layers to promote separation of concerns and reduce complexity.

answers.content: Use an AWS CodeCommit repository to host the dependencies in a centralized location.
answers.explanation: Using CodeCommit to host dependencies adds manual steps and complexity without leveraging Lambda layers for deployment efficiency.

questions.content:
A developer is modifying an existing AWS Lambda function. While checking the
code, the developer notices hardcoded parameter values for an Amazon RDS for SQL
Server user name, password, database, host, and port. There are also hardcoded
parameter values for an Amazon DynamoDB table, an Amazon S3 bucket, and an
Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

The developer wants to securely store the parameter values outside the code in
an encrypted format and wants to turn on rotation for the credentials. The
developer also wants to be able to reuse the parameter values from other
applications and to update the parameter values without modifying code.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an RDS database secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Set the user name, password, database, host, and port. Turn on secret rotation. Create encrypted Lambda environment variables for the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic.
answers.explanation: Uses encrypted Lambda environment variables for non-credential parameters, which is less reusable and harder to update without code changes.

answers.content: Create an RDS database secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Set the user name, password, database, host, and port. Turn on secret rotation. Create SecureString parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is best suited for storing and rotating RDS database credentials with minimal operational overhead. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameters provide encrypted storage for non-credential configuration values like DynamoDB table names, S3 buckets, and SNS topics. This approach guarantees secure storage, encrypted data, and enables rotation for credentials without code changes. It allows parameter reuse across other applications by centralizing the parameters and secrets. Options involving custom rotation logic add unnecessary operational overhead instead of leveraging managed services.

answers.content: Create RDS database parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the user name, password, database, host, and port. Create encrypted Lambda environment variables for the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic. Create a Lambda function and set the logic for the credentials rotation task. Schedule the credentials rotation task in Amazon EventBridge.
answers.explanation: Requires custom Lambda function and EventBridge scheduling for rotation, increasing operational overhead instead of using managed Secrets Manager rotation.

answers.content: Create RDS database parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the user name, password, database, host, and port. Store the DynamoDB table, S3 bucket, and SNS topic in Amazon S3. Create a Lambda function and set the logic for the credentials rotation. Invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.
answers.explanation: Uses S3 for storing configuration data and requires custom Lambda rotation, adding operational complexity and not using recommended managed services.

questions.content:
A mobile app stores blog posts in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Millions of posts
are added every day, and each post represents a single item in the table. The
mobile app requires only recent posts. Any post that is older than 48 hours can
be removed.

What is the MOST cost-effective way to delete posts that are older than 48
hours?

answers.content: For each item, add a new attribute of type String that has a timestamp that is set to the blog post creation time. Create a script to find old posts with a table scan and remove posts that are older than 48 hours by using the BatchWriteItem API operation. Schedule a cron job on an Amazon EC2 instance once an hour to start the script.
answers.explanation: Uses an EC2 instance with a cron job running a script that performs table scans, which is operationally expensive and not cost-effective for large-scale data.

answers.content: For each item, add a new attribute of type String that has a timestamp that is set to the blog post creation time. Create a script to find old posts with a table scan and remove posts that are older than 48 hours by using the BatchWriteItem API operation. Place the script in a container image. Schedule an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task on AWS Fargate that invokes the container every 5 minutes.
answers.explanation: Runs a containerized script on AWS Fargate frequently, incurring higher cost and complexity compared to using built-in TTL features.

answers.content: For each item, add a new attribute of type Date that has a timestamp that is set to 48 hours after the blog post creation time. Create a global secondary index (GSI) that uses the new attribute as a sort key. Create an AWS Lambda function that references the GSI and removes expired items by using the BatchWriteItem API operation. Schedule the function with an Amazon CloudWatch event every minute.
answers.explanation: Requires creating a GSI and frequent Lambda invocations with batch delete operations, which increase complexity and cost unnecessarily.

answers.content: For each item, add a new attribute of type Number that has a timestamp that is set to 48 hours after the blog post creation time. Configure the DynamoDB table with a TTL that references the new attribute.
answers.explanation: Using DynamoDB TTL to delete items based on an attribute that holds the expiration timestamp is the most cost-effective and operationally efficient method. TTL automatically removes expired items without requiring additional compute resources or manual intervention, reducing operational overhead and cost. This approach leverages a managed AWS service feature designed specifically for expiring and deleting items, aligning with best practices. Other options involve table scans and batch deletes that are expensive and inefficient for millions of items, and require running compute resources continuously or frequently.

questions.content:
A developer accesses AWS CodeCommit over SSH. The SSH keys configured to access
AWS CodeCommit are tied to a user with the following permissions:

[https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-developer-associate-dva-c02/image13.png]

The developer needs to create/delete branches.

Which specific IAM permissions need to be added, based on the principle of least
privilege?

answers.content: "codecommit:CreateBranch" "codecommit:DeleteBranch"
answers.explanation: The developer needs to create and delete branches specifically, so the least privilege approach requires only the permissions to create and delete branches. codecommit:CreateBranch and codecommit:DeleteBranch are the exact permissions required for these actions. Using only the necessary permissions aligns with IAM best practices to grant the minimum required permissions. Other broader permissions (Put*, Update*, *) grant more access than needed, violating least privilege principles.

answers.content: "codecommit:Put*"
answers.explanation: codecommit:Put* is broader and includes unrelated permissions beyond branch creation or deletion.

answers.content: "codecommit:Update*"
answers.explanation: codecommit:Update* does not explicitly grant create or delete branch permissions and is too broad.

answers.content: "codecommit:*"
answers.explanation: codecommit:* grants full access, violating least privilege by allowing unnecessary permissions.

questions.content:
An application that is deployed to Amazon EC2 is using Amazon DynamoDB. The
application calls the DynamoDB REST API. Periodically, the application receives
a ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error when the application writes to a
DynamoDB table.

Which solutions will mitigate this error MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Modify the application code to perform exponential backoff when the error is received.
answers.explanation: Correct; exponential backoff helps reduce throttling errors cost-effectively.

answers.content: Modify the application to use the AWS SDKs for DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Correct; AWS SDKs handle retries automatically, reducing throttling errors without extra cost.

answers.content: Increase the read and write throughput of the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: Increases cost and may be unnecessary if retries handle the issue.

answers.content: Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster for the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: DAX is mainly for read acceleration and adds cost; it does not directly solve write throughput exceeded errors.

answers.content: E. Create a second DynamoDB table. Distribute the reads and writes between the two tables.
answers.explanation: Distributing writes to a second table complicates application logic and does not cost-effectively solve throttling.

questions.content:
When a developer tries to run an AWS CodeBuild project, it raises an error
because the length of all environment variables exceeds the limit for the
combined maximum of characters.

What is the recommended solution?

answers.content: Add the export LC_ALL="en_US.utf8" command to the pre_build section to ensure POSIX localization.
answers.explanation: Setting localization does not address the environment variable length limit.

answers.content: Use Amazon Cognito to store key-value pairs for large numbers of environment variables.
answers.explanation: Amazon Cognito is not intended for storing environment variables or configuration data.

answers.content: Update the settings for the build project to use an Amazon S3 bucket for large numbers of environment variables.
answers.explanation: CodeBuild does not support using an S3 bucket directly for environment variable storage.

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store large numbers of environment variables.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store is designed to securely store configuration data and secrets, including environment variables, and can be integrated with CodeBuild. Using Parameter Store avoids hitting the combined character limit for environment variables within CodeBuild projects. Managed AWS services designed for secret and configuration management are preferred over custom or manual solutions, and Parameter Store is a managed service that suits this use case best. The given key facts emphasize CodeBuild environment variable usage and regional constraints but do not indicate S3 or Cognito as suitable for environment variable management.

questions.content:
A company is expanding the compatibility of its photo-sharing mobile app to
hundreds of additional devices with unique screen dimensions and resolutions.
Photos are stored in Amazon S3 in their original format and resolution. The
company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve the photos. The app
includes the dimension and resolution of the display as GET parameters with
every request.

A developer needs to implement a solution that optimizes the photos that are
served to each device to reduce load time and increase photo quality.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use S3 Batch Operations to invoke an AWS Lambda function to create new variants of the photos with the required dimensions and resolutions. Create a dynamic CloudFront origin that automatically maps the request of each device to the corresponding photo variant.
answers.explanation: Dynamic CloudFront origin mapping is complex and less preferred compared to Lambda@Edge routing for this use case.

answers.content: Use S3 Batch Operations to invoke an AWS Lambda function to create new variants of the photos with the required dimensions and resolutions. Create a Lambda@Edge function to route requests to the corresponding photo variant by using request headers.
answers.explanation: S3 Batch Operations with AWS Lambda is recommended to pre-create photo variants for known required dimensions, which is cost-effective compared to on-the-fly processing. Lambda@Edge allows routing requests based on headers (such as device dimensions) to the appropriate photo variant, optimizing delivery via CloudFront. This approach leverages CloudFront caching effectively by serving pre-processed images, reducing compute costs and latency. Options involving on-the-fly image processing at Lambda@Edge (C, D) are less cost-effective due to higher compute usage and latency. Dynamic origin mapping as in option A is complex and less suitable compared to Lambda@Edge for routing at edge locations.

answers.content: Create a Lambda@Edge function that optimizes the photos upon request and returns the photos as a response. Change the CloudFront TTL cache policy to the maximum value possible.
answers.explanation: On-the-fly image optimization at Lambda@Edge with maximum TTL lowers cache efficiency and increases cost and latency.

answers.content: Create a Lambda@Edge function that optimizes the photos upon request and returns the photos as a response. In the same function, store a copy of the processed photos on Amazon S3 for subsequent requests.
answers.explanation: Storing processed images back to S3 within Lambda@Edge is not a best practice and adds complexity and cost.

questions.content:
A company is building an application for stock trading. The application needs
sub-millisecond latency for processing trade requests. The company uses Amazon
DynamoDB to store all the trading data that is used to process each trading
request.

A development team performs load testing on the application and finds that the
data retrieval time is higher than expected. The development team needs a
solution that reduces the data retrieval time with the least possible effort.

Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Add local secondary indexes (LSIs) for the trading data.
answers.explanation: LSIs do not significantly improve retrieval latency to meet sub-millisecond requirements.

answers.content: Store the trading data in Amazon S3, and use S3 Transfer Acceleration.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration is not designed for low-latency, high-speed transactional data retrieval.

answers.content: Add retries with exponential backoff for DynamoDB queries.
answers.explanation: Retries with backoff help reliability but do not reduce latency and may increase response times.

answers.content: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache the trading data.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) provides a caching layer that reduces DynamoDB read latency to microseconds, which supports sub-millisecond latency requirements. Using DAX requires minimal changes to the application and is a managed service, thus aligning with the least possible effort criterion. Local secondary indexes improve query flexibility but do not explicitly reduce latency to sub-millisecond levels. Storing data in S3 and using Transfer Acceleration is not suitable for low-latency database queries. Retries with exponential backoff address transient errors and throttling but do not reduce data retrieval latency.

questions.content:
A developer is working on a Python application that runs on Amazon EC2
instances. The developer wants to enable tracing of application requests to
debug performance issues in the code.

Which combination of actions should the developer take to achieve this goal?
(Choose two.)

answers.content: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch agent collects logs and metrics but does not handle tracing for application requests.

answers.content: Install the AWS X-Ray daemon on the EC2 instances.
Configure the application to write JSON-formatted logs to /var/log/cloudwatch.
answers.explanation: Writing JSON-formatted logs to CloudWatch is unrelated to tracing, which requires X-Ray instrumentation.

answers.content: Configure the application to write trace data to /var/log/xray.
answers.explanation: Writing trace data to /var/log/xray is not the prescribed method; trace data should be sent via the X-Ray SDK and daemon.

answers.content: E. Install and configure the AWS X-Ray SDK for Python in the application.

questions.content:
A company has an application that runs as a series of AWS Lambda functions. Each
Lambda function receives data from an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon
SNS) topic and writes the data to an Amazon Aurora DB instance.

To comply with an information security policy, the company must ensure that the
Lambda functions all use a single securely encrypted database connection string
to access Aurora.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use IAM database authentication for Aurora to enable secure database connections for all the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: IAM database authentication enables secure, centralized, and encrypted database connection credentials management without hardcoding secrets. Using IAM authentication aligns with security best practices by avoiding credential storage and leveraging AWS managed authentication. The key facts describe permissions needed for RDS, Lambda, Secrets Manager, and IAM, indicating integration of managed services for secure access. Security best practices prioritize managed solutions like IAM authentication over storing credentials in environment variables or parameter store.

answers.content: Store the credentials and read the credentials from an encrypted Amazon RDS DB instance.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials on an encrypted RDS instance is not a standard or secure approach.

answers.content: Store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a secure string parameter.
answers.explanation: Though Parameter Store supports secure strings, AWS Secrets Manager is preferred for secrets management and rotation, and IAM DB authentication is more secure.

answers.content: Use Lambda environment variables with a shared AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for encryption.
answers.explanation: Environment variables, even encrypted with KMS, risk exposure if function configuration is accessed; not as secure as IAM authentication or Secrets Manager.

questions.content:
A developer is troubleshooting an Amazon API Gateway API. Clients are receiving
HTTP 400 response errors when the clients try to access an endpoint of the API.

How can the developer determine the cause of these errors?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to receive API call logs from API Gateway. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Logs as the delivery stream's destination.
answers.explanation: Using Kinesis Data Firehose with CloudWatch Logs as a destination is indirect and more complex for debugging API Gateway errors compared to directly enabling logging in API Gateway.

answers.content: Turn on AWS CloudTrail Insights and create a trail. Specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the trail for the stage of the API.
answers.explanation: AWS CloudTrail tracks API calls but is not designed for detailed troubleshooting of client HTTP 400 errors at the API Gateway endpoint level.

answers.content: Turn on AWS X-Ray for the API stage. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the log group for the API stage.
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray is better suited for tracing and debugging application code rather than directly identifying HTTP 400 error causes at API Gateway.

answers.content: Turn on execution logging and access logging in Amazon CloudWatch Logs for the API stage. Create a CloudWatch Logs log group. Specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the log group for the API stage.
answers.explanation: Execution logging and access logging in Amazon CloudWatch Logs directly capture detailed information about API Gateway requests and responses, including errors such as HTTP 400 responses. Creating and specifying a CloudWatch Logs log group for the API stage is a standard and secure practice to diagnose client errors. This approach uses managed AWS services designed for logs and monitoring, aligning with AWS best practices for operational troubleshooting.

questions.content:
A company developed an API application on AWS by using Amazon CloudFront, Amazon
API Gateway, and AWS Lambda. The API has a minimum of four requests every
second. A developer notices that many API users run the same query by using the
POST method. The developer wants to cache the POST request to optimize the API
resources.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure the CloudFront cache. Update the application to return cached content based upon the default request headers.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront can be configured to cache content including responses to POST requests when configured properly. API Gateway does not natively support caching POST requests at the method level. Using Lambda /tmp directory or Systems Manager Parameter Store for caching responses is a custom solution and does not align with AWS best practices for managed caching. CloudFront provides managed caching at edge locations and can optimize API resources effectively.

answers.content: Override the cache method in the selected stage of API Gateway. Select the POST method.
answers.explanation: API Gateway does not support caching for POST methods directly at the method level.

answers.content: Save the latest request response in Lambda /tmp directory. Update the Lambda function to check the /tmp directory.
answers.explanation: Caching in Lambda /tmp is a manual solution, less secure and less scalable than managed caching.

answers.content: Save the latest request in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Modify the Lambda function to take the latest request response from Parameter Store.
answers.explanation: Using Parameter Store for caching responses is not a secure or efficient managed caching mechanism.

questions.content:
A company is using AWS CloudFormation to deploy a two-tier application. The
application will use Amazon RDS as its backend database. The company wants a
solution that will randomly generate the database password during deployment.
The solution also must automatically rotate the database password without
requiring changes to the application.

What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

answers.content: Use an AWS Lambda function as a CloudFormation custom resource to generate and rotate the password.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function for password management requires custom code and maintenance, which is less operationally efficient and secure than using Secrets Manager.

answers.content: Use an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store resource with the SecureString data type to generate and rotate the password.
answers.explanation: Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString supports encryption but does not natively support automatic secret rotation.

answers.content: Use a cron daemon on the application's host to generate and rotate the password.
answers.explanation: A cron daemon on the application host is a manual, error-prone approach and not a managed service, thus failing on operational efficiency and best security practices.

answers.content: Use an AWS Secrets Manager resource to generate and rotate the password.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is designed to generate, store, and automatically rotate secrets such as database passwords. Using Secrets Manager avoids storing credentials in code or plaintext and provides managed rotation without manual intervention. This meets the requirement for automatic password generation during deployment and subsequent automatic rotation without application changes. Security best practices favor managed secret rotation services over custom or manual solutions.

questions.content:
A company is building a microservices application that consists of many AWS
Lambda functions. The development team wants to use AWS Serverless Application
Model (AWS SAM) templates to automatically test the Lambda functions. The
development team plans to test a small percentage of traffic that is directed to
new updates before the team commits to a full deployment of the application.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements in the MOST
operationally efficient way? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use AWS SAM CLI commands in AWS CodeDeploy to invoke the Lambda functions to test the deployment.
answers.explanation: AWS SAM CLI commands are used for local invoke and testing, not for directing traffic in deployment.

answers.content: Declare the EventInvokeConfig on the Lambda functions in the AWS SAM templates with OnSuccess and OnFailure configurations.
answers.explanation: EventInvokeConfig manages asynchronous invocation behaviors, not traffic shifting or gradual deployment.

answers.content: Enable gradual deployments through AWS SAM templates.
answers.explanation: Enabling gradual deployments alone is insufficient; specific deployment preferences and hooks are required to test and control traffic.

answers.content: Set the deployment preference type to Canary10Percent30Minutes. Use hooks to test the deployment.
E. Set the deployment preference type to Linear10PercentEvery10Minutes. Use hooks to test the deployment.

questions.content:
A developer has been asked to create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked any
time updates are made to items in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The function has
been created, and appropriate permissions have been added to the Lambda
execution role. Amazon DynamoDB streams have been enabled for the table, but the
function is still not being invoked.

Which option would enable DynamoDB table updates to invoke the Lambda function?

answers.content: Change the StreamViewType parameter value to NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES for the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: Changing StreamViewType alone does not enable the Lambda function to be invoked; it only controls what data is recorded in the stream.

answers.content: Configure event source mapping for the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB Streams must be explicitly mapped to the Lambda function using an event source mapping so that updates in the table trigger the Lambda function. Enabling DynamoDB Streams alone does not automatically invoke the Lambda function; setting up the event source mapping enables the integration. Other solutions like changing StreamViewType or using SNS are not necessary to invoke Lambda on table updates.

answers.content: Map an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to the DynamoDB streams.
answers.explanation: Mapping an SNS topic to DynamoDB Streams is not a standard or required way to invoke a Lambda function on table updates.

answers.content: Increase the maximum runtime (timeout) setting of the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Increasing the Lambda function timeout does not affect the invocation trigger behavior.

questions.content:
A developer needs to deploy an application running on AWS Fargate using Amazon
ECS. The application has environment variables that must be passed to a
container for the application to initialize.

How should the environment variables be passed to the container?

answers.content: Define an array that includes the environment variables under the environment parameter within the service definition.
answers.explanation: Environment variables cannot be specified under the environment parameter in the service definition.

answers.content: Define an array that includes the environment variables under the environment parameter within the task definition.
answers.explanation: Environment variables must be defined within the task definition to be passed to the container in an ECS Fargate environment. The environment parameter in the task definition is the correct place to specify environment variables according to AWS best practices. Defining environment variables in the service definition or using entryPoint parameters is not recommended or supported for this purpose. AWS recommends storing sensitive data in AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store, but environment variables themselves are specified in the task definition.

answers.content: Define an array that includes the environment variables under the entryPoint parameter within the task definition.
answers.explanation: The entryPoint parameter is not intended for specifying environment variables.

answers.content: Define an array that includes the environment variables under the entryPoint parameter within the service definition.
answers.explanation: The entryPoint parameter and service definition do not support environment variables.

questions.content:
A development team maintains a web application by using a single AWS RDS,
template. The template defines web servers and an Amazon RDS database. The team
uses the CloudFormation template to deploy the CloudFormation stack to different
environments.

During a recent application deployment, a developer caused the primary
development database to be dropped and recreated. The result of this incident
was a loss of data. The team needs to avoid accidental database deletion in the
future.

Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Add a CloudFormation DeletionPolicy attribute with the Retain value to the database resource.
Update the CloudFormation stack policy to prevent updates to the database.
Modify the database to use a Multi-AZ deployment.
answers.explanation: Multi-AZ deployment improves availability but does not prevent accidental deletion.

answers.content: Create a CloudFormation stack set for the web application and database deployments.
answers.explanation: Using a stack set does not inherently protect against accidental deletion of the database resource in a stack.

answers.content: E. Add a CloudFormation DeletionPolicy attribute with the Retain value to the stack.
answers.explanation: DeletionPolicy cannot be applied to the entire stack, only to individual resources.

questions.content:
A developer is storing sensitive data generated by an application in Amazon S3.
The developer wants to encrypt the data at rest. A company policy requires an
audit trail of when the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key was used and by
whom.

Which encryption option will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
answers.explanation: SSE-S3 uses Amazon S3 managed keys and does not provide an audit trail of key usage per company policy requirements.

answers.content: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS)
answers.explanation: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed keys (SSE-KMS) provides encryption at rest using KMS keys. SSE-KMS supports detailed audit trails through AWS CloudTrail, recording who used the key and when, meeting the audit trail requirement. Using AWS KMS (a managed service) aligns with AWS best practices for key management and security. Other options do not provide the required audit trail or full managed key lifecycle control.

answers.content: Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
answers.explanation: SSE-C requires customer-provided keys but does not integrate with AWS KMS for auditing, losing managed audit trail benefits.

answers.content: Server-side encryption with self-managed keys
answers.explanation: Self-managed keys are not a managed AWS service and do not provide built-in audit trail, increasing operational overhead and risk.

questions.content:
A company has an ecommerce application. To track product reviews, the company's
development team uses an Amazon DynamoDB table.

Every record includes the following:

• A Review ID, a 16-digit universally unique identifier (UUID)
• A Product ID and User ID, 16-digit UUIDs that reference other tables
• A Product Rating on a scale of 1-5
• An optional comment from the user

The table partition key is the Review ID. The most performed query against the
table is to find the 10 reviews with the highest rating for a given product.

Which index will provide the FASTEST response for this query?

answers.content: A global secondary index (GSI) with Product ID as the partition key and Product Rating as the sort key
answers.explanation: The most performed query is to find the top 10 reviews with the highest rating for a given product, which requires filtering by Product ID and sorting by Product Rating. A global secondary index (GSI) with Product ID as the partition key and Product Rating as the sort key allows efficient querying by the partition key (Product ID) and ordering by the sort key (Product Rating). Local secondary indexes (LSIs) share the same partition key as the base table, which is Review ID, so they cannot be used to query by Product ID efficiently. GSIs allow querying by attributes that differ from the base table's primary key, making a GSI on Product ID and Product Rating the best choice.

answers.content: A global secondary index (GSI) with Product ID as the partition key and Review ID as the sort key
answers.explanation: Sorting by Review ID does not support ordering reviews by their rating, which is required for the query.

answers.content: A local secondary index (LSI) with Product ID as the partition key and Product Rating as the sort key
answers.explanation: LSIs must have the same partition key as the base table (Review ID), so an LSI with Product ID as partition key is invalid.

answers.content: A local secondary index (LSI) with Review ID as the partition key and Product ID as the sort key
answers.explanation: LSI with Review ID as partition key does not support querying by Product ID, which is the key filter needed for the query.

questions.content:
A company needs to distribute firmware updates to its customers around the
world.

Which service will allow easy and secure control of the access to the downloads
at the lowest cost?

answers.content: Use Amazon CloudFront with signed URLs for Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront with signed URLs provides secure access control to Amazon S3 objects, ensuring only authorized customers can download the firmware. CloudFront signed URLs are a low-cost solution compared to creating multiple distributions or using Lambda functions. Using CloudFront integrates well with S3 storage and does not require complex custom access logic. Security best practices include controlling download access securely, which signed URLs provide.

answers.content: Create a dedicated Amazon CloudFront Distribution for each customer.
answers.explanation: Creating a dedicated CloudFront distribution per customer increases cost and complexity unnecessarily.

answers.content: Use Amazon CloudFront with AWS Lambda@Edge.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda@Edge adds operational overhead and cost without providing better access control compared to signed URLs.

answers.content: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to control access to an S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Using API Gateway and Lambda introduces more complexity and cost than CloudFront signed URLs for simple download access control.

questions.content:
A developer is testing an application that invokes an AWS Lambda function
asynchronously. During the testing phase, the Lambda function fails to process
after two retries.

How can the developer troubleshoot the failure?

answers.content: Configure AWS CloudTrail logging to investigate the invocation failures.
answers.explanation: CloudTrail logs API calls but does not capture failed asynchronous event payloads for Lambda processing.

answers.content: Configure Dead Letter Queues by sending events to Amazon SQS for investigation.
answers.explanation: Dead Letter Queues (DLQs) enable capturing and investigating events that failed asynchronous Lambda processing after retries. Using Amazon SQS as a DLQ is a managed AWS service solution to securely and reliably retain failed events for troubleshooting. Other options do not provide direct mechanisms for capturing and inspecting failed asynchronous events after retries. This approach aligns with best practices prioritizing secure and managed handling of failures over indirect or manual investigation.

answers.content: Configure Amazon Simple Workflow Service to process any direct unprocessed events.
answers.explanation: Amazon Simple Workflow Service is not designed for handling unprocessed asynchronous Lambda events.

answers.content: Configure AWS Config to process any direct unprocessed events.
answers.explanation: AWS Config is for compliance monitoring, not processing or analyzing failed Lambda asynchronous events.

questions.content:
A developer is creating a mobile application that will not require users to log
in.

What is the MOST efficient method to grant users access to AWS resources?

answers.content: Use an identity provider to securely authenticate with the application.
answers.explanation: Using an identity provider requires user authentication, which is not applicable since users do not log in.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function to create an IAM user when a user accesses the application.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users dynamically is inefficient, insecure, and violates best practices due to long-term credentials management.

answers.content: Create credentials using AWS KMS and apply these credentials to users when using the application.
answers.explanation: AWS KMS is used for encryption management, not for creating or managing credentials for user access to resources.

answers.content: Use Amazon Cognito to associate unauthenticated users with an IAM role that has limited access to resources.
answers.explanation: Amazon Cognito allows unauthenticated users to assume IAM roles with limited permissions efficiently, which is ideal for applications that do not require user login. Using Cognito ensures secure and managed access to AWS resources without creating individual IAM users or managing credentials manually. It aligns with AWS best practices of granting temporary, least-privilege access via managed services rather than creating long-term IAM users or handling credentials directly.

questions.content:
A company is migrating its PostgreSQL database into the AWS Cloud. The company
wants to use a database that will secure and regularly rotate database
credentials. The company wants a solution that does not require additional
programming overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for the database. Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on rotation.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store does not natively support automatic rotation of credentials without additional programming.

answers.content: Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for the database. Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on rotation.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is the appropriate database service for migrating a PostgreSQL database to AWS in a managed and compatible way. AWS Secrets Manager is specifically designed for managing secrets securely and supports automatic rotation without additional programming overhead. Using Secrets Manager aligns with AWS best practices to secure and regularly rotate database credentials. Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and not suitable for PostgreSQL migrations or relational database use cases.

answers.content: Use Amazon DynamoDB for the database. Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on rotation.
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is not a relational database and is incompatible with PostgreSQL migration requirements.

answers.content: Use Amazon DynamoDB for the database. Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on rotation.
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is not suitable for PostgreSQL migration despite using Secrets Manager for credentials.

questions.content:
A company has developed a new serverless application using AWS Lambda functions
that will be deployed using the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) CLI.

Which step should the developer complete prior to deploying the application?

answers.content: Compress the application to a .zip file and upload it into AWS Lambda.
answers.explanation: Directly zipping and uploading is not part of the SAM CLI deployment workflow

answers.content: Test the new AWS Lambda function by first tracing it in AWS X-Ray.
answers.explanation: Tracing the function with AWS X-Ray is useful but not a prerequisite for deployment

answers.content: Bundle the serverless application using a SAM package.
answers.explanation: Using AWS SAM requires running a packaging step to bundle and prepare the serverless application for deployment The SAM package step uploads local artifacts such as code and dependencies to an S3 bucket and generates a packaged template This step is necessary before running sam deploy to ensure the Lambda function and resources are correctly referenced and deployed

answers.content: Create the application environment using the eb create my-env command.
answers.explanation: The eb create command is related to AWS Elastic Beanstalk, not AWS SAM

questions.content:
A company wants to automate part of its deployment process. A developer needs to
automate the process of checking for and deleting unused resources that
supported previously deployed stacks but that are no longer used.

The company has a central application that uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit
(AWS CDK) to manage all deployment stacks. The stacks are spread out across
multiple accounts. The developer's solution must integrate as seamlessly as
possible within the current deployment process.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of
configuration?

answers.content: In the central AWS CDK application, write a handler function in the code that uses AWS SDK calls to check for and delete unused resources. Create an AWS CloudFormation template from a JSON file. Use the template to attach the function code to an AWS Lambda function and to invoke the Lambda function when the deployment stack runs.
answers.explanation: Uses a CloudFormation template from a JSON file, increasing complexity and not integrating as well with the CDK app.

answers.content: In the central AWS CDK application, write a handler function in the code that uses AWS SDK calls to check for and delete unused resources. Create an AWS CDK custom resource. Use the custom resource to attach the function code to an AWS Lambda function and to invoke the Lambda function when the deployment stack runs.
answers.explanation: Creating an AWS CDK custom resource integrates seamlessly with the current AWS CDK-based deployment process. The custom resource uses a Lambda function to perform the required checks and deletions programmatically. This approach avoids manual steps or separate management outside the CDK app, aligning with least configuration and automation needs.

answers.content: In the central AWS CDK, write a handler function in the code that uses AWS SDK calls to check for and delete unused resources. Create an API in AWS Amplify. Use the API to attach the function code to an AWS Lambda function and to invoke the Lambda function when the deployment stack runs.
answers.explanation: Using an AWS Amplify API is unrelated to deployment stacks and adds unnecessary complexity and configuration.

answers.content: In the AWS Lambda console, write a handler function in the code that uses AWS SDK calls to check for and delete unused resources. Create an AWS CDK custom resource. Use the custom resource to import the Lambda function into the stack and to invoke the Lambda function when the deployment stack runs.
answers.explanation: Writing Lambda code directly in the console is not integrated with the CDK app and requires manual Lambda creation, increasing configuration effort.

questions.content:
A company built a new application in the AWS Cloud. The company automated the
bootstrapping of new resources with an Auto Scaling group by using AWS
CloudFormation templates. The bootstrap scripts contain sensitive data.

The company needs a solution that is integrated with CloudFormation to manage
the sensitive data in the bootstrap scripts.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

answers.content: Put the sensitive data into a CloudFormation parameter. Encrypt the CloudFormation templates by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
answers.explanation: Storing sensitive data as CloudFormation parameters risks exposure since templates and parameters are not encrypted end-to-end securely; encrypting templates with KMS is not standard practice and does not protect parameter values during use.

answers.content: Put the sensitive data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the CloudFormation templates to download the object from Amazon S3 during bootstrap.
answers.explanation: Storing secrets in S3 risks exposure unless additional encryption and access controls are manually applied; this is less secure and not integrated with CloudFormation dynamic referencing.

answers.content: Put the sensitive data into AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a secure string parameter. Update the CloudFormation templates to use dynamic references to specify template values.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store supports secure string parameters that encrypt sensitive data. CloudFormation supports dynamic references to securely retrieve parameters from Systems Manager at stack creation time. Using secure strings in Parameter Store avoids embedding secrets directly in templates or parameters or storing in less secure locations. This approach aligns with AWS best practices prioritizing managed services designed for secret management and secure access. Other options either expose secrets in less secure ways or do not integrate securely with CloudFormation.

answers.content: Put the sensitive data into Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Enforce EFS encryption after file system creation. Update the CloudFormation templates to retrieve data from Amazon EFS.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EFS as a secret store is not a managed secret management service and complicates secure access; EFS encryption is applied after creation and does not provide integrated secret management.

questions.content:
A company needs to set up secure database credentials for all its AWS Cloud
resources. The company's resources include Amazon RDS DB instances, Amazon
DocumentDB clusters, and Amazon Aurora DB instances. The company's security
policy mandates that database credentials be encrypted at rest and rotated at a
regular interval.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

answers.content: Set up IAM database authentication for token-based access. Generate user tokens to provide centralized access to RDS DB instances, Amazon DocumentDB clusters, and Aurora DB instances.
answers.explanation: IAM database authentication supports token-based access but does not manage or rotate credentials themselves.

answers.content: Create parameters for the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Set the Type parameter to SecureString. Set up automatic rotation on the parameters.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store SecureString encrypts secrets but does not natively support automatic secret rotation.

answers.content: Store the database access credentials as an encrypted Amazon S3 object in an S3 bucket. Block all public access on the S3 bucket. Use S3 server-side encryption to set up automatic rotation on the encryption key.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials in an encrypted S3 object is less secure and violates best practices; S3 does not provide automatic rotation or secret management features.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function by using the SecretsManagerRotationTemplate template in the AWS Secrets Manager console. Create secrets for the database credentials in Secrets Manager. Set up secrets rotation on a schedule.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager provides managed secret storage with encryption at rest by default. Secrets Manager supports automated secret rotation using Lambda functions, meeting the requirement for regular rotation. Secrets Manager is designed specifically for managing secrets securely compared to other options like Parameter Store or S3. Managed rotation by Secrets Manager follows security best practices while minimizing manual intervention.

questions.content:
A developer has created an AWS Lambda function that makes queries to an Amazon
Aurora MySQL DB instance. When the developer performs a test, the DB instance
shows an error for too many connections.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

answers.content: Create a read replica for the DB instance. Query the replica DB instance instead of the primary DB instance.
answers.explanation: Creating a read replica does not reduce the number of connections to the primary DB and does not address connection pool management.

answers.content: Migrate the data to an Amazon DynamoDB database.
answers.explanation: Migrating to DynamoDB is a major change and increases operational effort; it is not a minimal-effort fix for connection issues.

answers.content: Configure the Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
answers.explanation: Multi-AZ deployment is for availability and failover, not for managing connection limits or reducing simultaneous connections.

answers.content: Create a proxy in Amazon RDS Proxy. Query the proxy instead of the DB instance.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy is a managed service designed to pool and share database connections, reducing the number of connections to the database and managing connection limits. Using RDS Proxy offloads the connection management from the Lambda functions, reducing operational effort and directly addressing the 'too many connections' error. Other options do not directly solve the connection limit problem with the least operational effort or do not align with best practices for managing database connections.

questions.content:
A developer is creating a new REST API by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS
Lambda. The development team tests the API and validates responses for the known
use cases before deploying the API to the production environment.

The developer wants to make the REST API available for testing by using API
Gateway locally.

Which AWS Serverless Application Model Command Line Interface (AWS SAM CLI)
subcommand will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Sam local invoke
answers.explanation: 'sam local invoke' is used to invoke Lambda functions directly, not to simulate the entire API Gateway locally.

answers.content: Sam local generate-event
answers.explanation: 'sam local generate-event' produces event JSON for different Lambda triggers and does not start a local API server.

answers.content: Sam local start-lambda
answers.explanation: 'sam local start-lambda' starts a local endpoint to run Lambda functions but does not simulate API Gateway endpoints.

answers.content: Sam local start-api
answers.explanation: The 'sam local start-api' command allows you to run your API Gateway REST API locally for testing purposes. It supports hot reloading, enabling quick development and iteration by refreshing only changed files without losing application state. This subcommand is designed specifically to start the API locally and make it available for testing, meeting the developer's requirement.

questions.content:
A company has a serverless application on AWS that uses a fleet of AWS Lambda
functions that have aliases. The company regularly publishes new Lambda function
by using an in-house deployment solution. The company wants to improve the
release process and to use traffic shifting. A newly published function version
should initially make available only to a fixed percentage of production users.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure routing on the alias of the new function by using a weighted alias.
answers.explanation: Routing on the alias of the new function by using a weighted alias allows traffic shifting between Lambda function versions. The weighted alias approach supports directing a fixed percentage of traffic to the new version as required. This method aligns with the fact that you can point an alias to a maximum of two Lambda function versions and distribute traffic probabilistically. Using weighted aliases is the standard and most straightforward way to implement traffic shifting for Lambda versions.

answers.content: Configure a canary deployment type for Lambda.
answers.explanation: Canary deployment is a deployment strategy concept, not a direct Lambda configuration option; the question asks for a specific solution using AWS Lambda features.

answers.content: Configure routing on the new versions by using environment variables.
answers.explanation: Using environment variables for routing does not enable traffic shifting or weighted routing between Lambda versions.

answers.content: Configure a linear deployment type for Lambda.
answers.explanation: Linear deployment is a deployment strategy similar to canary but not directly selectable configuration in Lambda for traffic shifting; weighted alias is the correct Lambda native mechanism.

questions.content:
A company has an application that stores data in Amazon RDS instances. The
application periodically experiences surges of high traffic that cause
performance problems. During periods of peak traffic, a developer notices a
reduction in query speed in all database queries.

The team's technical lead determines that a multi-threaded and scalable caching
solution should be used to offload the heavy read traffic. The solution needs to
improve performance.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST complexity?

answers.content: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to offload read requests from the main database.
answers.explanation: Memcached is less feature-rich and less preferred over Redis for complex and scalable caching needs.

answers.content: Replicate the data to Amazon DynamoDSet up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster.
answers.explanation: Replicating data to DynamoDB and setting up DAX involves data migration and additional service complexity, not the least complex solution.

answers.content: Configure the Amazon RDS instances to use Multi-AZ deployment with one standby instance. Offload read requests from the main database to the standby instance.
answers.explanation: Multi-AZ standby instances do not serve read traffic; they are passive and only used for failover, so this does not offload read traffic.

answers.content: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to offload read requests from the main database.
answers.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is a fully managed, multi-threaded, and scalable caching solution designed to offload read traffic and improve database performance. ElastiCache for Redis supports complex data structures and provides high throughput and low latency, which aligns with the requirement to handle surges of high traffic efficiently. Using a managed caching service is less complex than data replication or custom solutions, and better suited than Multi-AZ standby instances which are meant for failover rather than read scaling.

questions.content:
A developer must provide an API key to an AWS Lambda function to authenticate
with a third-party system. The Lambda function will run on a schedule. The
developer needs to ensure that the API key remains encrypted at rest.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Store the API key as a Lambda environment variable by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key.
answers.explanation: Storing the API key as a Lambda environment variable encrypted with a customer-managed AWS KMS key ensures the secret is encrypted at rest by design. Using AWS KMS for encryption aligns with AWS best practices for managing secrets securely without embedding them in code. AWS Secrets Manager or AWS KMS integration with Lambda environment variables provides a managed approach over manual solutions or insecure methods.

answers.content: Configure the application to prompt the user to provide the password to the Lambda function on the first run.
answers.explanation: Prompting the user for a password on the first run is not feasible for scheduled Lambda functions with no user interaction.

answers.content: Store the API key as a value in the application code.
answers.explanation: Storing the API key directly in application code is insecure and violates AWS best practices by exposing secrets in plaintext.

answers.content: Use Lambda@Edge and only communicate over the HTTPS protocol.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda@Edge and HTTPS only secures data in transit but does not address encryption of the API key at rest.

questions.content:
An IT department uses Amazon S3 to store sensitive images. After more than 1
year, the company moves the images into archival storage. The company rarely
accesses the images, but the company wants a storage solution that maximizes
resiliency. The IT department needs access to the images that have been moved to
archival storage within 24 hours.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive provides the lowest cost option for archival storage with standard retrieval in 9 to 48 hours, which meets the 24-hour access requirement. S3 Standard-IA is suitable for infrequent access storage before archiving, balancing cost and availability. Using S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval is more aligned with the 24-hour retrieval need compared to bulk retrieval, which takes longer. S3 One Zone-IA is less resilient than S3 Standard-IA and is not recommended for sensitive images requiring maximum resiliency.

answers.content: Use S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with bulk retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: Bulk retrieval from Glacier Deep Archive takes 5 to 12 hours, but standard retrieval is more appropriate since the requirement is access within 24 hours and bulk retrieval is typically for slower, less frequent access; also standard retrieval is recommended for timely access.

answers.content: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is more expensive than S3 Standard-IA for infrequent access and the question requires cost-effectiveness; intelligent-tiering also may not provide cost savings for long-term archival use before Glacier Deep Archive.

answers.content: Use S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with bulk retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA provides less resiliency as data is stored in a single availability zone, which is against the requirement to maximize resiliency.

questions.content:
An IT department uses Amazon S3 to store sensitive images. After more than 1
year, the company moves the images into archival storage. The company rarely
accesses the images, but the company wants a storage solution that maximizes
resiliency. The IT department needs access to the images that have been moved to
archival storage within 24 hours.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is suitable for storing infrequently accessed but important data with high resiliency across multiple AZs. S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval provides retrieval within 12 hours, meeting the requirement to access images within 24 hours. Using Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval is more cost-effective than faster retrieval options and aligns with the need for rare access. S3 One Zone-IA is less resilient as it stores data in a single AZ, which does not maximize resiliency. Bulk retrievals from Glacier Deep Archive can take up to 48 hours, exceeding the 24-hour access requirement. S3 Intelligent-Tiering can optimize cost automatically but is designed for frequent access patterns and managing cost between frequent and infrequent access, not specifically for long-term archival.

answers.content: Use S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with bulk retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: Bulk retrieval from Glacier Deep Archive can take up to 48 hours, which fails the 24-hour access requirement.

answers.content: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with standard retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is not the best cost-effective choice for data intended for archival after a year and requiring retrieval within 24 hours.

answers.content: Use S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) to store the images. Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive with bulk retrieval to store and retrieve archived images.
answers.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA lacks the resiliency across multiple Availability Zones needed for the sensitive images.

questions.content:
A developer is building a serverless application by using the AWS Serverless
Application Model (AWS SAM). The developer is currently testing the application
in a development environment. When the application is nearly finished, the
developer will need to set up additional testing and staging environments for a
quality assurance team.

The developer wants to use a feature of the AWS SAM to set up deployments to
multiple environments.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

answers.content: Add a configuration file in TOML format to group configuration entries to every environment. Add a table for each testing and staging environment. Deploy updates to the environments by using the sam deploy command and the --config-env flag that corresponds to each environment.
answers.explanation: AWS SAM supports the use of a TOML configuration file to group configuration entries for different deployment environments. Using the --config-env flag allows easy deployment of updates to specific environments without creating multiple templates or custom scripts. This approach minimizes development effort by leveraging native AWS SAM CLI features designed for multi-environment deployments.

answers.content: Create additional AWS SAM templates for each testing and staging environment. Write a custom shell script that uses the sam deploy command and the --template-file flag to deploy updates to the environments.
answers.explanation: Creating multiple SAM templates and custom scripts increases development and maintenance effort unnecessarily.

answers.content: Create one AWS SAM configuration file that has default parameters. Perform updates to the testing and staging environments by using the --parameter-overrides flag in the AWS SAM CLI and the parameters that the updates will override.
answers.explanation: Using --parameter-overrides requires manual parameter specification each time and is more error-prone and less manageable than using config-env.

answers.content: Use the existing AWS SAM template. Add additional parameters to configure specific attributes for the serverless function and database table resources that are in each environment. Deploy updates to the testing and staging environments by using the sam deploy command.
answers.explanation: Adding multiple parameters and handling environment-specific attributes manually complicates deployment and lacks the streamlined environment grouping that the SAM config file provides.

questions.content:
A developer is working on an application that processes operating data from IoT
devices. Each IoT device uploads a data file once every hour to an Amazon S3
bucket. The developer wants to immediately process each data file when the data
file is uploaded to Amazon S3.

The developer will use an AWS Lambda function to process the data files from
Amazon S3. The Lambda function is configured with the S3 bucket information
where the files are uploaded. The developer wants to configure the Lambda
function to immediately invoke after each data file is uploaded.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Add an asynchronous invocation to the Lambda function. Select the S3 bucket as the source.
answers.explanation: Asynchronous invocation is not the mechanism to trigger Lambda directly from S3 uploads.

answers.content: Add an Amazon EventBridge event to the Lambda function. Select the S3 bucket as the source.
answers.explanation: EventBridge events do not directly handle S3 object upload triggers for immediate Lambda invocation.

answers.content: Add a trigger to the Lambda function. Select the S3 bucket as the source.
answers.explanation: The requirement is to immediately invoke the Lambda function after each file upload to S3. S3 bucket triggers for Lambda are the standard method to invoke Lambda functions in response to S3 object upload events. EventBridge is not used for direct S3 object upload event triggers for Lambda. Asynchronous invocation or layers do not inherently connect S3 uploads to Lambda invocations. The provided facts mention the creation of Lambda functions and S3 events but state that existing S3 event-based functions cannot be reused for batch operations, which is separate from the immediate invocation requirement.

answers.content: Add a layer to the Lambda function. Select the S3 bucket as the source.
answers.explanation: Lambda layers are used to include additional code or dependencies, not for event source configuration.

questions.content:
A developer is setting up infrastructure by using AWS CloudFormation. If an
error occurs when the resources described in the Cloud Formation template are
provisioned, successfully provisioned resources must be preserved. The developer
must provision and update the CloudFormation stack by using the AWS CLI.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Add an --enable-termination-protection command line option to the create-stack command and the update-stack command.
answers.explanation: --enable-termination-protection prevents deletion of the stack, not rollback on errors during creation or update.

answers.content: Add a --disable-rollback command line option to the create-stack command and the update-stack command.
answers.explanation: Using the --disable-rollback option when creating or updating a CloudFormation stack prevents CloudFormation from rolling back successfully provisioned resources if an error occurs during provisioning. This option preserves the resources that have been successfully created despite the error, meeting the requirement to retain resources upon failure. Other options such as --enable-termination-protection help prevent stack deletion but do not affect rollback behavior on errors. Parameters or tags named PreserveResources have no impact on rollback behavior in CloudFormation.

answers.content: Add a --parameters ParameterKey=PreserveResources,ParameterValue=True command line option to the create-stack command and the update-stack command.
answers.explanation: There is no CloudFormation parameter named PreserveResources that influences resource retention on errors.

answers.content: Add a --tags Key=PreserveResources,Value=True command line option to the create-stack command and the update-stack command.
answers.explanation: Tags have no effect on provisioning error handling or rollback behavior.

questions.content:
A developer is building a serverless application that connects to an Amazon
Aurora PostgreSQL database. The serverless application consists of hundreds of
AWS Lambda functions. During every Lambda function scale out, a new database
connection is made that increases database resource consumption.

The developer needs to decrease the number of connections made to the database.
The solution must not impact the scalability of the Lambda functions.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure provisioned concurrency for each Lambda function by setting the ProvisionedConcurrentExecutions parameter to 10.
answers.explanation: Provisioned concurrency controls warm Lambda instances but does not reduce database connections or connection pooling.

answers.content: Enable cluster cache management for Aurora PostgreSQL. Change the connection string of each Lambda function to point to cluster cache management.
answers.explanation: Cluster cache management is not a recognized feature of Aurora PostgreSQL for connection pooling and does not reduce database connections.

answers.content: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a connection pool to manage the database connections. Change the connection string of each Lambda function to reference the proxy.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy is a fully managed service designed to pool and share database connections efficiently. RDS Proxy reduces the number of open connections to the Aurora PostgreSQL database, which prevents database resource exhaustion during Lambda scale out. Using RDS Proxy does not limit the scalability of Lambda functions because it manages connections transparently and securely without imposing restrictive concurrency limits. Other options either do not address connection management appropriately or limit Lambda scalability (e.g., provisioned or reserved concurrency).

answers.content: Configure reserved concurrency for each Lambda function by setting the ReservedConcurrentExecutions parameter to 10.
answers.explanation: Reserved concurrency limits the number of concurrent Lambda executions, affecting scalability rather than managing database connections.

questions.content:
A developer is preparing to begin development of a new version of an
application. The previous version of the application is deployed in a production
environment. The developer needs to deploy fixes and updates to the current
version during the development of the new version of the application. The code
for the new version of the application is stored in AWS CodeCommit.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: From the main branch, create a feature branch for production bug fixes. Create a second feature branch from the main branch for development of the new version.
answers.explanation: Creating separate branches from the main branch for production bug fixes and for new version development aligns with Git best practices for managing concurrent development and production fixes. Using branches allows parallel, isolated workstreams without impacting each other, which is critical for production stability and ongoing development. The provided facts reference use of Git and CodeCommit core concepts but do not support use of tags for change management or new repositories for development. Applying restrictive IAM policies on branches is not a standard or practical workflow for managing development and production fixes.

answers.content: Create a Git tag of the code that is currently deployed in production. Create a Git tag for the development of the new version. Push the two tags to the CodeCommit repository.
answers.explanation: Tags are not appropriate for managing ongoing development and hotfix branches since tags mark specific commits and are immutable.

answers.content: From the main branch, create a branch of the code that is currently deployed in production. Apply an IAM policy that ensures no other users can push or merge to the branch.
answers.explanation: IAM policies restricting pushes or merges to specific branches is not a common or effective method for branch management or concurrent development streams.
